texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Isolated rainfall and thunderstorms resulted in varying amounts of precipitation over the past week with accumulations ranging from 0.9 mm to 65.1 mm (Table 1). Most regions received more than 6 mm of rain. Sprague Lake received the most rain this week with 65.1 mm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to June 22 range from 93.4 mm to 157.8 mm (Table 2) and are based on 30-year historical data. Even with recent rainfall, the East, Interlake and large parts of the Northwest have accumulations under 60% of normal. While accumulations in the Southwest and parts of the Central regions are closer to normal, only a few locations have accumulated more than 90% of the 30-year average since May 1.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Much needed moisture in the southwest region has provided a significant boost to crop development.
texts.text: Much needed moisture in the southwest region has provided a significant boost to crop development.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter cereals are performing well, and fungicide applications on winter wheat have been completed. Spring wheat is generally in the tillering to stem elongation stages, with some early-seeded fields beginning to head. Barley and oats are in the tillering to stem elongation stages. Corn is in the V5 stage.
texts.text: Winter cereals are performing well, and fungicide applications on winter wheat have been completed. Spring wheat is generally in the tillering to stem elongation stages, with some early-seeded fields beginning to head. Barley and oats are in the tillering to stem elongation stages. Corn is in the V5 stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola ranges from the 2 leaf stage to pre-bolting. Flax is currently 10 to 15 cm tall. Sunflowers are in the V4 to V6 stage.
texts.text: Canola ranges from the 2 leaf stage to pre-bolting. Flax is currently 10 to 15 cm tall. Sunflowers are in the V4 to V6 stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Peas are progressing well, and most fields are at the 10 to 12 node stage. Flowering is expected to begin later this week, and producers are preparing to apply fungicides for disease control. Soybeans are at the V3 to V5 stage.
texts.text: Peas are progressing well, and most fields are at the 10 to 12 node stage. Flowering is expected to begin later this week, and producers are preparing to apply fungicides for disease control. Soybeans are at the V3 to V5 stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Herbicide applications are complete in spring cereals and producers are preparing for disease control. In-crop herbicide applications are approximately 80% complete in soybeans, dry beans and corn. Herbicide applications continue in sunflower and late seeded canola.
texts.text: Herbicide applications are complete in spring cereals and producers are preparing for disease control. In-crop herbicide applications are approximately 80% complete in soybeans, dry beans and corn. Herbicide applications continue in sunflower and late seeded canola.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The entire Northwest region received precipitation this week. Overnight temperatures remained cool, with The Pas station recording the lowest temperature at 7°C. Herbicide applications continue as crop stages are reached.
texts.text: The entire Northwest region received precipitation this week. Overnight temperatures remained cool, with The Pas station recording the lowest temperature at 7°C. Herbicide applications continue as crop stages are reached.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter wheat crops are wrapping up the flowering stage. The most advanced spring wheat is at the beginning of head emergence and the remainder of the crop is in the tillering to stem elongation stage.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat crops are wrapping up the flowering stage. The most advanced spring wheat is at the beginning of head emergence and the remainder of the crop is in the tillering to stem elongation stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas are growing well, and recent rains will benefit the crops. Most field peas are in the vegetative stage with the most advanced moving into the R1 stage. Where moisture is lacking, some crops appear short. Soybeans are in the V2 to V3 stage.
texts.text: Field peas are growing well, and recent rains will benefit the crops. Most field peas are in the vegetative stage with the most advanced moving into the R1 stage. Where moisture is lacking, some crops appear short. Soybeans are in the V2 to V3 stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola varies across the region. Depending on seeding date and moisture conditions for germination, crop stages vary greatly. Earliest seeded crops are in the rosette stage and near bolting. The remainder of the crops continue behind, ranging from 2 to 6 leaf.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rains were welcome across the Central region, with most falling in the south. Overall, crops appear to be in good condition. Most crops have recovered from earlier issues such as soil crusting, frost, and high winds.
texts.text: Rains were welcome across the Central region, with most falling in the south. Overall, crops appear to be in good condition. Most crops have recovered from earlier issues such as soil crusting, frost, and high winds.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye are advancing quickly, and FHB fungicide is being applied. Spring cereals are booting and the earliest fields have heads emerged. Fungicide applications in spring cereals will start when the crop reaches the appropriate stage. Corn ranges from V4 to V7 and many producers have completed a second herbicide application.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye are advancing quickly, and FHB fungicide is being applied. Spring cereals are booting and the earliest fields have heads emerged. Fungicide applications in spring cereals will start when the crop reaches the appropriate stage. Corn ranges from V4 to V7 and many producers have completed a second herbicide application.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola ranges from early rosette to early flowering. Herbicide applications are complete for most fields but some later seeded fields are still being sprayed.
texts.text: Canola ranges from early rosette to early flowering. Herbicide applications are complete for most fields but some later seeded fields are still being sprayed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas are exhibiting strong growth and uniform emergence. The most advanced fields are at early flowering. The most advanced soybeans have reached the 6 th trifoliate, although some fields are as early as the 3 rd trifoliate. Some minor cases of iron deficiency chlorosis being reported. However, the crop is growing out of the symptoms.

The most advanced soybeans have reached the 6 th trifoliate, although some fields are as early as the 3 rd trifoliate. Some minor cases of iron deficiency chlorosis being reported. However, the crop is growing out of the symptoms.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall across the Eastern region was welcome, with areas further to the East receiving the most rainfall.
texts.text: Rainfall across the Eastern region was welcome, with areas further to the East receiving the most rainfall.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spring cereals are looking good, with fields in the boot to early heading stage on average. Some plant growth regulators (PGR) were applied, but with the drier conditions, it is expected that less PGR's were used this season. FHB fungicides will start soon depending on crop development. On average, corn is in the V4 to V6 stage and producers are wrapping up second pass herbicide applications.
texts.text: Spring cereals are looking good, with fields in the boot to early heading stage on average. Some plant growth regulators (PGR) were applied, but with the drier conditions, it is expected that less PGR's were used this season. FHB fungicides will start soon depending on crop development. On average, corn is in the V4 to V6 stage and producers are wrapping up second pass herbicide applications.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola generally varies from rosette to early flowering. Producers are wrapping up canola herbicide applications.
texts.text: Canola generally varies from rosette to early flowering. Producers are wrapping up canola herbicide applications.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The soybean crop varies due to some late seeded fields and emergence issues. Soybeans are in the 3 rd to 6 th trifoliate stage and second pass herbicide applications are wrapping up. Some iron deficiency chlorosis has been noted, but the crop appears to be growing out of the symptoms. With summer solstice behind us soybeans are expected to reach R1 stage within a week to ten days.

Some iron deficiency chlorosis has been noted, but the crop appears to be growing out of the symptoms. With summer solstice behind us soybeans are expected to reach R1 stage within a week to ten days.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas are in the V7 to V10 stage.
texts.text: Field peas are in the V7 to V10 stage.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall over much of the region was welcome, although amounts were variable. Crops are generally looking good, although some fields are beginning to show signs of stress due to the warm and dry conditions. Very dry conditions continue in parts of the Interlake.
texts.text: Rainfall over much of the region was welcome, although amounts were variable. Crops are generally looking good, although some fields are beginning to show signs of stress due to the warm and dry conditions. Very dry conditions continue in parts of the Interlake.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The majority of spring cereals are in the flag to boot stage, with several fields starting to show awns. Fungicide applications for FHB are expected to begin as the crops reach the appropriate stage. Winter wheat and fall rye are advancing quickly, with most advanced fields starting to set seed. Corn is in the V4 to V6 stage, with the majority of herbicide applications complete.

Corn is in the V4 to V6 stage, with the majority of herbicide applications complete.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Early seeded canola ranges from bolting to early flower. Canola crop quality ranges across the region. Some fields have good stands and others are thin and stagey due to earlier stresses including frost injury, flea beetle damage
